messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: prior conditional on explanatory variable
parts:
Stan users:

Did anybody had experience to model prior conditional on explanatory variable in stan?  Problem looks very simple - to have prior more informative in some regions and less informative in other regions.  Basically I want to model experimental data via y~a+b*f(x)+eps, eps~N(0,sigma).  Around x=0.5 from physical considerations prior of a should be very informative and close to zero while b should be close to 1.  The prior should be vague in other regions. 

Linas

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] prior conditional on explanatory variable
parts:
Do the x and y go together, say indexed by n, so that the
model is

y[n] = a + b * f(x[n]) + epsilon[n]
epsilon[n] ~ normal(0,sigma)

or equivalently

y[n] ~ normal(a + b * f(x[n]), sigma);

What I'm missing is how a and b depend on x[n].

- Bob

messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: Re: prior conditional on explanatory variable
parts:
The model could be:
y[n] ~ normal(a(x[n]) + b(x[n]) * f(x[n]), sigma);
where a(x)=c*(1-exp(-(0.5-x)^2) and b(x)=d*exp(-(0.5-x)^2).  Perhaps there could be something better than exp(-x^2)?
